figures.title: Per-query speedups at SF1
figures.caption_draft: Per-query speedup t_ref / t_engine at SF1 for the four primary contrasts. Dots are geometric means over rounds, thick bars the 95% t-interval on the mean log-ratio (df = rounds − 1), thin bars the minimum and maximum round. The bottom row of each panel is the suite geometric mean over the queries available for both sides. Marker shape and colour name the engine whose speedup is shown (C4: the better GPU engine in most rounds). Queries an engine cannot complete are written out in the panel (✗ not supported and OOM out of memory are coverage outcomes; ◐ unstable coverage, a coverage outcome in some rounds only, is excluded from every estimate by A1; ! is an integrity failure that should not occur in accepted rounds) and are excluded from the suite row.
figures.alt_text: Forest plots of per-query speedups at SF1 for each contrast and suite.

figures.title: GPU coverage matrix
figures.caption_draft: Support of each query on the two GPU engines at every scale, across the included rounds. Polars GPU runs under raise_on_fail=True, so a query it cannot execute entirely on the GPU is a recorded failure, never a CPU timing. Failure classes differ in fill, glyph and lightness: violet ✗ operation not supported on the GPU, amber OOM device or host out of memory (both coverage outcomes, A1), dark red ! any other error, which is an integrity failure that fails its round and so should not occur in accepted rounds; a hatched cell is unstable coverage (A1): the coverage outcome occurred in some rounds only (k of n rounds ran) and the cell is excluded from every contrast in all rounds. cx_q13 (inline regex flag) and cx_window (cum_count over a window) were declared unsupported before the campaign; black-outlined cells are failures that were not.
figures.alt_text: Matrix of supported, unsupported, out-of-memory and other-error cells for Polars GPU and Spark GPU by query and scale factor.

figures.title: Position and carryover effects
figures.caption_draft: Mean deviation of log time from each cell's own mean over rounds, by session position within a (suite, scale) block (left/top) and by the engine that ran immediately before (right/bottom). figures.title: GPU memory versus scale
figures.caption_draft: Device memory by engine and scale factor; what is measured differs by engine. Polars GPU: nvidia-smi device memory of the worker process during the timed action, maximum over the three trials and the included rounds. cudf-polars allocates through an RMM async pool that retains freed blocks, so this is the pool's high-water mark in the session so far (it never falls within a session in 32 of 32 sessions) and an upper bound on what a query needs, not a per-query working set. Spark GPU: the largest device allocation any single task reported (RAPIDS task accumulator gpuMaxDeviceMemoryBytes in the Spark event log) among the tasks launched inside the action; it is not a simultaneous total over concurrent tasks. The nvidia-smi sample of the Spark process tree is constant within only 0 of 32 sessions, so it is not a reservation line and is not drawn. Lines are medians over queries and bands the range; the solid horizontal line is the device's memory.
figures.alt_text: GPU memory against scale factor for Polars GPU and Spark GPU, one panel per suite.
